summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex history of sclerosing mesenteritis, chronic small bowel obstructions, and prior abdominal surgeries was readmitted for recurrent abdominal pain, nausea, and failure to pass flatus, consistent with a functional small bowel obstruction. She was managed conservatively with bowel rest, NG tube decompression, and TPN. After no improvement over the first week, a small bowel follow-through and push enteroscopy showed slow transit without a transition point, confirming a functional obstruction. A G-tube was placed for long-term decompression and hydration via free water flushes. During her stay, she developed transient word-finding difficulties and subjective right-sided weakness; neurologic workup including CT head and CTA head/neck showed no acute findings, with changes attributed to a prior stroke. Her anticoagulation was transitioned from rivaroxaban to therapeutic enoxaparin due to concerns about absorption. Pain was managed with Dilaudid suppositories, and she was discharged home on TPN, G-tube care, and follow-up plans with a new GI surgeon and specialists.
